meta.title: Retirement Simulator — Monte Carlo Retirement Planning
meta.description: Stress-test your retirement plan against thousands of simulated market futures. Free, private, and it runs entirely in your browser.

hero.badge: Monte Carlo engine · runs in your browser
hero.subtitle: The engine replays your whole financial life through thousands of simulated markets — volatility, inflation, pension, and spending — so you see the full range of outcomes before you bet your retirement on a single guess.
hero.note: No sign-up. No cloud. Your data never leaves this browser.
hero.lede: One average return tells you nothing.

The same plan on your own dashboard runs {defaultRuns} paths by default and reports {defaultRate} — fewer samples, same plan. Raise the run count in the plan editor whenever you want a tighter answer.

features.title: Everything a serious plan needs
features.subtitle: A complete planning engine — no spreadsheet gymnastics required.

monteCarlo.title: A real Monte Carlo engine
monteCarlo.body: Lognormal returns sampled with the Box–Muller transform — thousands of complete market lifetimes, computed in seconds.

live.title: Instant what-if answers
live.body: Move any slider and the percentiles redraw in about 100 milliseconds. Interrogate every assumption, live.

phases.title: Both halves of the journey
phases.body: Accumulation to drawdown in one model: savings growth, statutory pension, one-time windfalls, and custom expense streams.

reports.title: Reports worth sharing
reports.body: Export a clean, comprehensive PDF of your plan — assumptions, charts, and recommendations included.

privacy.title: Private by design
privacy.body: No account and no tracking of your finances. Parameters persist only in your browser's local storage.

bilingual.title: Bilingual & localized
bilingual.body: Full English and German interfaces with proper currency, number, and date formatting throughout.

how.title: From guess to plan in five minutes

monthlyPension.tooltip: Expected monthly pension from the government system, starting at legal retirement age. This reduces your required private savings.

oneTimeIncomes.tooltip: Add lump-sum inflows such as insurance payouts, home sales, or inheritances. These are invested at the start of the year following the age you choose.

capitalGainsTax.label: Abgeltungsteuer (capital gains tax)
capitalGainsTax.tooltip: German flat tax on realised investment gains, including solidarity surcharge — 26.375% for most savers. Only the gains portion of a sale is taxed.

averageROI.label: Average ROI
averageROI.tooltip: Expected annual return on investments. Historical stock market: ~7-10%. Bond portfolio: ~3-5%. Diversified portfolio: ~6-8%.

roiVolatility.label: ROI Volatility
roiVolatility.tooltip: Standard deviation of returns. Higher volatility means more uncertainty. Conservative: 5-10%, Moderate: 10-15%, Aggressive: 15-25%.

averageInflation.label: Average Inflation
averageInflation.tooltip: Expected annual inflation rate. ECB target: 2%. Historical average in developed countries: 2-3%.

inflationVolatility.label: Inflation Volatility
inflationVolatility.tooltip: How much inflation varies year-to-year. Historical range: 0.5-1.5%. Higher volatility creates more uncertainty in retirement costs.

simulationRuns.label: Number of Runs
simulationRuns.tooltip: Monte Carlo simulations to run. More runs = higher accuracy but slower computation. 1000+ recommended for reliable results.

withdrawalStrategy.label: Withdrawal Strategy
withdrawalStrategy.tooltip: Four rules for turning a portfolio into an income. They trade spending stability against the chance of running out — the planner below shows both.

fixedReal.label: Fixed real spending
fixedReal.description: Spend the same purchasing power every year — steady income, highest risk of running dry.

vanguardDynamic.label: Dynamic with guardrails (Vanguard)
vanguardDynamic.description: Follow the portfolio, but never cut below the floor or raise above the ceiling.

guytonKlinger.label: Guyton-Klinger guardrails
guytonKlinger.description: Inflation raises as usual, plus a 10% cut or raise once the withdrawal rate drifts 20% off course.

percentOfPortfolio.label: Percent of portfolio
percentOfPortfolio.description: Spend a fixed share of the portfolio each year — it can never run dry, but income swings with the market.

dsWithdrawalRate.label: Withdrawal rate
dsWithdrawalRate.tooltip: Vanguard: the rate targeted each year. Guyton-Klinger: the initial rate the guardrails are measured against. Percent of portfolio: the rate spent outright.

dsCeilingRate.label: Spending ceiling
dsCeilingRate.tooltip: Largest raise versus last year’s inflation-adjusted spending.

dsFloorRate.label: Spending floor
dsFloorRate.tooltip: Largest cut versus last year’s inflation-adjusted spending.

marketModel.label: Market model
marketModel.tooltip: Monte Carlo draws returns from your assumptions. Historical replays a real return series year by year.

monteCarlo.label: Monte Carlo
monteCarlo.description: Random draws from your return, volatility and inflation assumptions.

historical.label: Historical
historical.description: Replays real market history — one path per available start year.

marketModel.historicalNotice: Historical mode supplies returns, volatility and inflation from the record itself ({count} start years, {from}–{to}), so the assumptions below are ignored while it is on.
marketModel.runsIgnored: Fixed at {count} in historical mode — one path per start year, not a sample.
marketModel.leverIgnored: Ignored in historical mode — returns come from the record.

glidePath.label: Glide path
glidePath.description: Slide from equities into bonds as retirement approaches, then hold that mix.
glidePath.correlationNote: The two sleeves are blended assuming zero correlation between equities and bonds: the blended volatility is √(w²σe² + (1−w)²σb²). Real stock/bond correlation swings either side of zero, so a blended plan may look slightly calmer here than it would in practice.
glidePath.historicalNote: In historical mode these assumptions are ignored: the allocation is applied to each year’s actual equity and bond returns.

note.fixedReal: Rows show every retirement year under fixed real spending: the configured expenses rise with simulated inflation and are not adjusted for portfolio performance. The pension offsets how much of the median allowance must come from the portfolio.
note.vanguardDynamic: Rows show every retirement year under the Vanguard guardrails: the first year starts from the plan, then target spending is {withdrawalRate} of the prior year-end portfolio, bounded by the {ceiling} / {floor} guardrails against inflation-adjusted prior spending. The pension does not set the allowance; it offsets how much of it must come from the portfolio.
note.guytonKlinger: Rows show every retirement year under Guyton-Klinger: spending is inflation-linked, cut by 10% whenever the withdrawal rate runs more than 20% above {withdrawalRate} and raised by 10% whenever it runs more than 20% below. The pension offsets how much of the allowance must come from the portfolio.
note.percentOfPortfolio: Rows show every retirement year under percent of portfolio: spending is {withdrawalRate} of the prior year-end portfolio, with no memory of last year. The pension offsets how much of the allowance must come from the portfolio.

strategies.fixedReal: Fixed real spending keeps the planned budget on an inflation path. Portfolio returns decide whether the withdrawals succeed, but they never change what is spent.

success.title: Success rate definition
success.description: A simulation run is considered successful if the portfolio maintains a positive balance through the entire planning horizon (age {age}). The success rate represents the percentage of all simulation runs that meet this criterion.

items.distribution: Returns are assumed to follow a normal distribution, which may not capture extreme market events
items.inflationModel: Inflation is modeled as constant in real terms across all expense categories
items.taxPolicy: Tax rates and regulations are assumed to remain constant
items.unexpected: No consideration for unexpected one-time expenses or windfalls
items.healthcare: Healthcare costs may increase faster than general inflation
items.pension: Pension benefits assumed to be inflation-adjusted and guaranteed

monteCarlo.definition: Statistical technique using random sampling to model uncertainty

successRate.definition: Percentage of simulations where portfolio lasts through planning horizon

sequenceRisk.definition: Risk that poor returns early in retirement significantly impact outcomes

planningHorizon.definition: The age through which the plan projects (life expectancy assumption)

switcher.limit: Plan limit reached ({max}). Delete a plan to add another.

new.title: New plan
new.description: Starts from your current parameters. Edit it without touching your other plans.
new.label: Plan name

duplicate.title: Duplicate plan
duplicate.description: Copies “{name}” — including any unsaved edits — into a new plan and switches to it.
duplicate.label: Name for the copy

rename.title: Rename plan
rename.description: Give this plan a name you will recognise later.
rename.label: Plan name

delete.title: Delete this plan?
delete.description: “{name}” and its parameters will be removed. This cannot be undone.

wizard.title: Save this plan
wizard.description: Name what you just configured so you can compare it against other plans later.
wizard.label: Plan name

scenario.title: Save as new plan
scenario.description: Creates a new plan from “{source}” with this lever applied. Your current plan stays active.
scenario.label: Plan name
scenario.noChanges: This lever leaves the parameters unchanged.

comparison.title: Compare plans
comparison.subtitle: Run two or three plans side by side to see what each choice really costs.
comparison.hint: Select {min}–{max} plans, then run the comparison.
comparison.needMorePlans: Create a second plan to unlock side-by-side comparison.
comparison.empty: No comparison yet — pick your plans and press run.
comparison.error: Comparison could not be completed. Please try again.
comparison.runsNote: Path counts used: {detail}. Recomputed only when you press the button.

chart.title: Median assets by age

chart.aria: Line chart overlaying the median asset path of each compared plan by age.

comparison.stale: Parameters changed since this comparison ran — run it again for current numbers.
comparison.emptyReady: {count} plans are already selected — press “Run comparison” to line them up.
comparison.emptyNeedsSelection: Select at least {min} plans, then run the comparison.
comparison.selectMore: Select at least {min} plans — a comparison needs two to say anything.

assumptions.title: Assumptions
assumptions.description: The inputs behind these numbers. Rows that differ are highlighted.
assumptions.identical: These plans share every assumption we compare — only the run-to-run noise differs.

comparison.selectionChanged: Selection changed since this comparison ran — run it again for the plans you picked.
comparison.staleDirty: The active plan has unsaved edits — this row still shows the saved plan.

toasts.planCreatedFrom: Created “{name}” from “{source}” — selected in Compare plans.

dirty.hint: These edits drive the simulation but are not stored in this plan yet.

switchGuard.title: Unsaved changes in “{name}”
switchGuard.description: You edited “{name}” without saving. Choose what happens before switching to “{target}”.

deleted.restoreFailed: Could not restore the plan — the plan limit is reached.

headerControls.title: Display settings
headerControls.description: Switch the interface language or pick a different visual theme.

planEditor.title: Plan assumptions
planEditor.description: Every input “{name}” simulates. Edits run live and stay in the working copy until you save them to the plan.
planEditor.descriptionGeneric: Every input this plan simulates. Edits run live and stay in the working copy until you save them to the plan.

personal.title: Personal & timeline
personal.description: The ages that frame saving and drawdown.

income.title: Income & savings
income.description: What flows in before and after you stop working.

expenses.title: Expenses
expenses.description: What this plan has to fund, every year.

cashFlows.description: Everything this plan pays out or takes in, and for how long.

summary.pensionsHint: {count, plural, =0 {no pension} =1 {# pension} other {# pensions}} · gross per month

reset.title: Reset THIS plan to defaults?
reset.description: Every assumption in “{name}” goes back to the default scenario. Your other plans are untouched, and nothing is stored until you save this plan.

goals.title: Legacy goal
goals.description: What this plan should still be worth at the end, in today's euros.
goals.targetHelp: In today's purchasing power. 0 means the plan only has to last — nothing has to be left over.
goals.disabled: No legacy goal: a run succeeds as long as the money lasts.
goals.fundedHint: Never depletes and clears the target
goals.fundedHintNoGoal: No goal set — this is plain survival

sections.staleStats: A value below is out of range — these figures still describe the last accepted entry.

quickAdjust.title: Quick what-if
quickAdjust.description: The four levers that move the outcome most. Every change lands in the working copy.
quickAdjust.expensesHint: Scales the {count} lifetime expenses in this plan ({total}/mo) proportionally.
quickAdjust.expensesHintScheduled: Scales the {count} lifetime expenses ({total}/mo) proportionally. The {scheduled} scheduled flows with an age window are not affected — edit those in the Plan tab.

withdrawalPlanner.title: Withdrawal planner
withdrawalPlanner.description: How this plan turns a portfolio into a monthly income — and what that income is allowed to do when markets misbehave.
withdrawalPlanner.noParams: This strategy has no settings: it simply spends the plan’s budget, inflation-linked.

stats.firstYearHint: Median monthly spending at age {age}, today’s €
stats.floorHint: Least this rule can pay at age {age}, today’s €
stats.volatilityHint: P90 ÷ P10 of real spending at age {age}
stats.successHint: Share of futures that met the plan’s goal

withdrawalPlanner.tradeoff: A lower spread means a more predictable income; a higher success rate means less chance of running out. Move the rate and watch both move.

corridor.title: Spending corridor
corridor.description: The shaded band is where 80% of simulated futures land. The dashed lines are not a forecast: they are what the rule itself promises, whatever the market does.
corridor.caveat: The floor holds as long as the portfolio does — it is a rule, not a guarantee from a third party.
corridor.noFloor: This strategy promises no floor: set one below to put a hard bottom under your income.
corridor.empty: Run the simulation to see the corridor.
corridor.aria: Spending corridor from age {retirementAge}: median spending with the P10–P90 band and the strategy’s planned floor and ceiling.

compare.title: Compare all four strategies
compare.subtitle: Same plan, same market paths, four withdrawal rules. This is the trade-off, in numbers.
compare.error: The strategy comparison failed. Please try again.
compare.empty: Run the comparison to see all four strategies side by side.
compare.stale: The plan changed since this comparison ran.
compare.runsNote: Each strategy is run over the same {runs} market paths, so the differences are the rules and nothing else. Lifetime spending is the median path summed in today’s euros; the spread is P90 ÷ P10 at age {age}.
